source.title: Signed Input Regularization
source.authors: Saeid Asgari Taghanaki; Kumar Abhishek; G. Hamarneh

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the full paper; some equations and figure content are garbled, but the reported classification results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests a new input regularization method on natural-label classification tasks and reports held-out performance; it does not test any listed version directly.
record.gate_note: The paper compares SIGN with other augmentation methods on natural-label classification. It does not test random-label memorization, width, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, optimizer choice, batch size, dropout effects, generalization measures, or removal of memorized examples. Its out-of-distribution and corruption results are outside the claim’s scope.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates SIGN input augmentation. It cites dropout and batch-size generalization findings as background but neither tests nor relies on any listed version as an experimental tool. Held-out performance alone does not test the specific comparisons in V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: iterative SIGN augmentation can improve generalization and achieves higher classification performance than the evaluated alternatives in their experiments. These conclusions concern SIGN, not V1–V8.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces Jacobian-based SIGN input transformations as a data augmentation regularizer; the listed claim versions concern other interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and model differ across experiments; on CIFAR-10 the reported overall accuracy varies across augmentation methods. The paper also evaluates distinct out-of-distribution and corruption settings, which do not bear on the claim’s in-distribution generalization versions.

fits_no_version.finding: SIGN raises MobileNetV2 CIFAR-10 accuracy from 0.8550 to 0.8637 and Inception-ResNet-v2 ISIC test AUC from 0.7611 to 0.7787.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SIGN input augmentation can improve held-out image-classification performance in the tested settings.

record.problems: The paper reports held-out classification accuracy or AUC rather than training and test error together, so it cannot establish the size of a generalization gap. Uncertainty estimates are not stated for the classification comparisons in R1 and R2.
record.rows_left_out: Out-of-distribution Tiny ImageNet results and corrupted-input results in Sections 3.3 and Tables 3 and 5 are omitted because the claim excludes out-of-distribution behavior and those corruption conditions. Transferability results in Table 4 compare training with SIGN-transformed samples but do not report a baseline-to-SIGN comparison on the same model-training setup relevant to the claim.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and changes that mitigate them.
Effects of adding, removing, or varying dropout. BasicCNN's dropout probability is fixed at 0.3.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The absence of training-test gaps is not the main exclusion: several versions concern held-out performance directly, but their required interventions or comparisons are absent here. The record's explanation for excluding Table 4 is inaccurate: it does provide a NASNetMobile classical-versus-transferred-SIGN comparison, 0.8085 versus 0.8478. It remains outside all listed versions and was already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and held-out performance on natural labels for the same architectures and recipes.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
Dropout is not varied or isolated; its presence in BasicCNN is part of the architecture.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or comparison of generalization measures.
No memorized-example identification, removal, or retraining experiment.

rows.subject: MobileNetV2
rows.stage_stated: trained for 100 epochs; selected epoch with highest validation accuracy
rows.operation_detail: Training with SIGN input regularization versus classical data augmentation on CIFAR-10; reports mean classification accuracy.
rows.note: Natural-label test performance comparison; this does not measure the training-test error gap.
rows.check: The values are correct: MobileNetV2 accuracy increases from 0.8550 with classical augmentation to 0.8637 with SIGN. This is the study's own method comparison and measures no listed version; its observed state cannot describe a claim-version effect.

rows.subject: Inception-ResNet-v2
rows.operation_detail: Training with SIGN input regularization and comparing test-set AUC with the baseline model without data augmentation.
rows.note: The paper describes the test-set improvement as approximately 2%; no test error or train-test gap is reported.
rows.check: The test AUC values, 0.7611 and 0.7787, are correct. This is the study's own SIGN-versus-baseline comparison and measures no listed version. The increase does not warrant a partial state for any version. Section 3 specifies 100 training epochs and validation-based epoch selection for this model.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
